sections.purpose: The Daily Protein Target is an educational screening aid that estimates a daily protein intake target — grams per day, grams per kilogram and a per-meal split — for healthy adults from published population guidelines. It is not a prescription, not a diagnosis and not individualised clinical nutrition advice.
sections.who: Adults aged 18 to 99 with healthy kidney function. If you report kidney disease the tool gives no numeric target, because national kidney guidelines recommend a reduced, supervised protein intake. Pregnancy and breastfeeding use their own recommended-allowance branch. Liver disease and the recovery goal are flagged as clinical and shown with a clinician-referral message. The tool is not for children, dialysis patients or people under medical nutrition therapy.
sections.enter:
• Age and sex
  • Height and weight (metric or imperial)
  • Ethnicity (sets the healthy-weight cut-offs)
  • General activity level and resistance training
  • Your goal and how you eat
  • Kidney and liver health questions
sections.limitations:
• Population guideline figures, not individual requirements: the tool does not account for kidney function tests, protein quality, energy balance or medical conditions beyond the yes/no questions it asks.
  • The plant-diet multipliers (1.1 vegetarian, 1.2 vegan) are an extrapolation from digestibility literature, not a guideline figure.
  • Targets are capped at 2.0 g/kg; higher intakes described in the literature apply to supervised, trained individuals only.

Read the medical disclaimer and when to seek urgent care.
sections.how: The tool collects the guideline bands that apply to you (Institute of Medicine RDA and AMDR, International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand, Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, PROT-AGE for older adults, ESPEN for illness and recovery), takes the most demanding applicable band, applies a diet-quality multiplier and caps the result at 2.0 g/kg. Engine: Lifeline Daily Protein Target engine (published-band lookup). Deployed version [lld_tool_version slug="protein"].
sections.privacy: The calculation runs in your browser. Nothing you enter is stored on our servers. If you choose to email yourself the result, the e-mail is sent once and not kept; see our Privacy Policy.

sections.purpose: The Diabetes Risk Check is an educational screening aid that estimates your 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes from self-reported, non-laboratory inputs, and encourages a conversation with a clinician or an NHS Health Check where indicated. It does not diagnose diabetes, type 1 diabetes or any other condition.
sections.who: Adults aged 25 to 84 without a diagnosis of diabetes. Age is entered as a five-year band. Classic symptoms trigger a same-day-assessment banner; the emergency checklist suppresses the percentage and directs you to urgent care. The tool is not a diagnosis.
sections.enter:
• Age band and sex
  • Height, weight and (optionally) waist
  • Ethnicity and smoking
  • Family history and medical history
  • Current symptoms, checked separately from the score
sections.limitations:
• QDiabetes-2018 was derived and validated in UK primary-care populations; calibration for visitors outside the UK is not established.
  • The Townsend deprivation score is fixed at a neutral average, which can under- or over-state risk for individual visitors.
  • Band labels and thresholds (5.6 %, 10 %, 20 %) are interpretation cut-points chosen by Lifeline Daily.

Read the medical disclaimer and when to seek urgent care.
sections.how: The score is the published QDiabetes-2018 (Model A) algorithm, calibrated in the UK, which uses a deprivation score we hold fixed and estimates type 2 diabetes risk; symptoms are handled separately from the number. Waist-to-height ratio and the Indian Diabetes Risk Score are shown as cross-checks. Engine: QDiabetes-2018 (Model A). Deployed version [lld_tool_version slug="diabetes"].
sections.privacy: The calculation runs in your browser. Nothing you enter is stored on our servers. If you choose to email yourself the result, the e-mail is sent once and not kept; see our Privacy Policy.

disclaimer.title: Medical Disclaimer & Urgent Care
disclaimer.content:
Screening, not diagnosis

The Lifeline Daily health tools give general information and screening estimates from published methods. A result is not a diagnosis and does not replace advice from a doctor, nurse, dietitian or pharmacist who knows your history.

When to seek urgent care

If you feel very unwell — for example vomiting, drowsiness or confusion, fast or deep breathing, chest pain, or stomach pain — get a same-day medical assessment. Do not wait for a screening result.

  • United Kingdom: call 999 in an emergency, or NHS 111 for urgent advice.
  • Sri Lanka: call 1990 (Suwa Seriya ambulance).
  • India: call 112.
  • Elsewhere, call your local emergency number.

What the tools cannot do

The tools use only the answers you give. They cannot see your blood tests, medicines or medical history, and they are not designed for children, pregnancy-specific care beyond what each tool states, or people under specialist care for kidney or liver disease. Each tool page lists its own limitations.

Contact

Questions about these pages or the tools: contact us. Privacy: see our Privacy Policy.
